explanation: I found no Mathlib declaration stating this result. `kyFanSum` (the sum of the k largest singular values, i.e. the Ky Fan k-norm) is defined in the library itself. I searched Mathlib for `kyFan`, `KyFan` and `singularValues`. The only hits are `Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/SingularValues.lean` and `NormDet.lean`. I listed every theorem in `SingularValues.lean`: they cover only basic facts, such as nonnegativity, antitonicity, support and the zero operator. None of them is a triangle inequality for sums of the top-k singular values (the Ky Fan inequality). The library's own proof reduces the claim to its square-matrix version, `kyFanSum_add_le_square`, using its own `zeroExtension` lemmas, so it does not rely on any Mathlib result of this kind.
